expectations.text: Output identifies random negative sampling as a key validity problem (easy negatives inflate AUROC by 10-20pp)
expectations.evidence: Problem 2 section explicitly describes easy random negatives: 'most of your negatives are pairs of nodes with no common neighbors, in different communities, possibly in different components — these are trivially easy to distinguish from real friendships.' Correcting it is said to 'drop AUROC another 5–15 points'.

expectations.text: Output specifically identifies GNN message-passing leakage: test edges are visible in the message-passing graph during node encoding, so the model effectively 'sees' the test answers while training
expectations.evidence: Problem 1 section states: 'If test edge (A, B) is present in the training adjacency matrix during message passing, node A's embedding encodes information about B's neighborhood, and vice versa. When you then ask "will A and B connect?", the GNN already knows they are connected — it was in the training graph.' and 'The test edges are still visible to the encoder.' This precisely describes the message-passing leakage mechanism.

expectations.text: Output recommends a temporal train/test split (train on edges before time T, evaluate on edges after T) as the correct evaluation for the stated temporal forecasting goal
expectations.evidence: The 'Temporal validity' checklist and 'The correct evaluation pipeline' section both specify: 'Temporal split: train on edges formed before cutoff T; test on edges formed in the 6-month window after T. This is the only way to simulate real deployment.'

expectations.text: Output recommends comparing to a simple structural baseline (Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, or Common Neighbors) as a required sanity check
expectations.evidence: A dedicated 'Baseline sanity check' section recommends Adamic-Adar as 'The single most informative diagnostic,' provides full Python code for computing it, and states 'Baselines to beat: Adamic-Adar and Resource Allocation on the same temporal split and same hard negatives.'

expectations.text: Output recommends hard negative sampling (distance-2 non-edges or structurally similar non-edges) as a required fix
expectations.evidence: The fix for Problem 2 explicitly recommends 'hard negatives — non-edges that share at least one common neighbor' and 'sample negatives from node pairs at graph distance exactly 2 (one hop away from being connected).' The correct evaluation pipeline also specifies 'sample non-edges at-time-T with at least one common neighbor (distance-2 pairs), stratified by degree.'
